questions.q: What specifically breaks about naming files report_v2_FINAL.py once more than one person is working on a project?
options: It makes the file load slower
There's no record of who changed what or why, and two people editing at once can silently overwrite each other's work
Python refuses to run files with underscores in the name
It only breaks if the file is over 1MB
questions.explain: Manual copies have no tracked history and no protection against two people's edits clobbering each other.

questions.q: What is a "commit" in version control terms?
options: A saved, timestamped, attributed snapshot of the project at a point in time
A synonym for deleting a file
A password required to open the repository
A type of merge conflict
questions.explain: A commit is the core unit of history in a VCS — a recorded snapshot you can always return to.

questions.q: Which of these is something a version control system gives you that manually copying files does not?
options: Faster internet speeds
Automatic code formatting
The ability to revert to any previous snapshot, with a record of who made each change and when
Free cloud storage
questions.explain: Recoverability and attributed history are the core benefits a VCS adds over ad hoc file copies.

questions.q: What does it mean that Git is a "distributed" version control system?
options: It only works when connected to the internet
Every developer's clone holds the full project history, not just a central server
It distributes your code publicly by default
It requires a separate server for every branch
questions.explain: Unlike older centralized systems, every Git clone is a full copy of the repository's history, which is why Git works offline.

questions.q: Why does this course spend Chapters 1–2 on Git itself before covering GitHub's collaboration features?
options: GitHub requires a separate paid license to use Git
Git is being deprecated in favor of GitHub
GitHub's features (pull requests, code review, issues) are built on top of Git, which is the version control system nearly every team and GitHub itself are built around
Git and GitHub are unrelated products with no connection
questions.explain: GitHub is a hosting and collaboration layer built on top of Git — understanding Git first makes GitHub's features make sense.
